# Comprehensive Learning Guide: Implementing ToDo App with PHP Symfony

## Course Overview

This intermediate-level course teaches you how to build a fully functional ToDo application using the **PHP Symfony framework**, one of the most robust and industry-standard frameworks in modern PHP development. You'll progress from foundational Symfony concepts through building a complete, production-ready application with authentication, data validation, testing, and REST API capabilities.

**Who this course is for:**
- PHP developers transitioning from procedural code to modern frameworks
- Backend engineers preparing for mid-level positions at tech companies
- Full-stack developers wanting to solidify backend architecture skills
- Developers already familiar with MVC concepts but new to Symfony's ecosystem

**Why it matters for interview prep:**
Symfony is widely used in enterprise environments and interviews often test your ability to work within opinionated frameworks, understand dependency injection, handle security concerns, and architect scalable applications. Mastering this path demonstrates maturity in real-world backend development beyond basic CRUD operations.

---

## Core Topics Covered

- **Symfony Architecture & Project Setup** – Project structure, configuration, environment management, service container, and dependency injection
- **Routing & Controllers** – Request/response cycle, controller best practices, parameter converters, and HTTP methods
- **Doctrine ORM & Database Design** – Entity mapping, migrations, relationships (One-to-One, One-to-Many, Many-to-Many), and query optimization
- **Forms & Validation** – Form types, constraints, custom validators, and error handling
- **Authentication & Authorization** – User providers, password encoding, role-based access control (RBAC), and security firewalls
- **Templating with Twig** – Template inheritance, macros, filters, and view logic
- **Testing (Unit & Functional)** – PHPUnit integration, fixture management, and API testing
- **REST API Development** – JSON responses, serialization, versioning, and API best practices

---

## Learning Path Workflow

### **Phase 1: Symfony Fundamentals (Tasks 1–12)**
Start here to understand Symfony's architecture and conventions.

1. Install Symfony and explore project structure
2. Understand service container and dependency injection
3. Configure environment variables and settings
4. Create your first controller and route
5. Understand the request/response lifecycle
6. Set up basic routing with parameters
7. Learn about Symfony console commands
8. Configure database connection
9. Understand the lifecycle of a Symfony application
10. Set up local development environment properly
11. Learn about bundles and extensions
12. Practice: Build a static page with multiple routes

### **Phase 2: Database Layer with Doctrine (Tasks 13–24)**
Build the data persistence foundation for your ToDo app.

13. Create your first Entity (Task/Todo)
14. Define entity properties and data types
15. Generate database migrations
16. Execute migrations and verify schema
17. Create a User entity with relationships
18. Define One-to-Many relationship (User → Tasks)
19. Create repository classes and custom queries
20. Write DQL (Doctrine Query Language) queries
21. Implement eager loading to avoid N+1 queries
22. Create fixtures for testing data
23. Handle cascading deletes and orphan removal
24. Practice: Design complete database schema with migrations

### **Phase 3: Forms & Validation (Tasks 25–32)**
Implement robust user input handling.

25. Create a TaskType form class
26. Implement form rendering in Twig templates
27. Add built-in validators (NotBlank, Length, Email, etc.)
28. Create custom validators
29. Handle form submission and validation errors
30. Implement conditional validation (groups)
31. Add CSRF protection to forms
32. Practice: Build complete form workflow with error display

### **Phase 4: Authentication & Security (Tasks 33–39)**
Secure your application and control access.

33. Set up user provider and authenticator
34. Implement password encoding strategy
35. Create login form and authentication route
36. Set up security firewall configuration
37. Implement role-based access control
38. Protect routes with access control rules
39. Practice: Build complete auth system with login/logout/register

### **Phase 5: Building the Core ToDo Features (Tasks 40–48)**
Implement the main application logic.

40. Create task creation functionality
41. Implement task listing with filtering
42. Add task editing capability
43. Implement task deletion with confirmation
44. Add task status/completion toggling
45. Implement task prioritization
46. Add due date functionality
47. Create task categories/tags
48. Practice: Complete working ToDo app with all CRUD operations

### **Phase 6: API & Advanced Features (Tasks 49–54)**
Extend functionality with REST capabilities.

49. Create API endpoints returning JSON
50. Implement serialization with symfony/serializer
51. Add API pagination and filtering
52. Implement API versioning strategy
53. Add API documentation (OpenAPI/Swagger)
54. Practice: Build complete REST API for ToDo app

### **Phase 7: Testing & Deployment (Tasks 55–58)**
Ensure quality and prepare for production.

55. Write unit tests for repository queries
56. Write functional tests for controllers
57. Implement integration tests for full workflows
58. Practice: Deploy application and write performance tests

---

## Key Skills You'll Build

### **Architecture & Design**
- Understanding the dependency injection container and service configuration
- Building scalable application structure following SOLID principles
- Separating concerns between controllers, services, repositories, and entities
- Recognizing and implementing design patterns (Repository, Factory, Strategy)

### **Database Mastery**
- Designing normalized relational schemas
- Creating and managing migrations effectively
- Writing efficient Doctrine queries with joins and filtering
- Understanding performance implications (N+1 queries, lazy loading, eager loading)
- Managing database transactions and data consistency

### **Web Development Fundamentals**
- Full request/response lifecycle in a web framework
- HTTP method semantics (GET, POST, PUT, DELETE, PATCH)
- Proper URL routing and parameter extraction
- Content negotiation and response formatting (HTML, JSON)

### **Security Consciousness**
- Implementing authentication flows securely
- Password handling and encoding best practices
- CSRF protection and XSS prevention
- Authorization and access control patterns
- Understanding common vulnerabilities (SQLi, CSRF, XSS)

### **Testing & Quality Assurance**
- Writing meaningful unit tests with proper isolation
- Functional testing of web endpoints
- Test fixtures and database transaction management
- Measuring and improving code coverage

---

## Sample Problem Types

### **Problem Type 1: Entity Relationships & Complex Queries**

**Description:** Design entities for a ToDo system where users have multiple projects, each project has multiple tasks, tasks can have subtasks, and tasks can be tagged. Query all incomplete tasks for a user across all projects, ordered by priority and due date.

class User {
    #[ORM\OneToMany(targetEntity: Project::class, mappedBy: 'user')]
    private Collection $projects;
}

// Entity: Project

class Project {
    #[ORM\ManyToOne(targetEntity: User::class)]
    private User $user;
    
    #[ORM\OneToMany(targetEntity: Task::class, mappedBy: 'project', cascade: ['remove'])]
    private Collection $tasks;
}
